hyperparameters.name: N (consecutive time steps for state)
hyperparameters.context: State representation for the DRL method, where matrices of consecutive time steps are stacked to form the state.
hyperparameters.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st: St = {mt-(N-1),..., mt}.

hyperparameters.name: Uv (constant for vehicle representation)
hyperparameters.context: Used in the position matrix to represent vehicles in the control area.
hyperparameters.source_quote: mt(x, y) = Uv, i E It, where Uv is a constant

metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a com-puting server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic video data from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, used as inputs for the deep reinforcement learning method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract and preprocess video traffic data
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices. The proposed method takes the preprocessed video data as inputs...
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are extracted from raw traffic video frames. These locations are used to create position matrices representing the traffic state at each time step. Consecutive matrices are stacked to capture vehicle dynamics, and the stacked matrices are down-sampled to reduce input dimensions. Signal state information is also included in the position matrix.

nodes_process.node_name: Train Deep Q-Network for ramp metering
nodes_process.source_quote: We propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method... We adopt a deep neural network termed Q-network to approximate Q* (s, a)... The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: A Deep Q-Network (DQN) is trained to approximate the optimal action-value function Q*(s,a) for ramp metering. The network uses convolutional and fully connected layers. Training employs experience replay, a target network, an epsilon-greedy strategy for action selection, and a multitask learning approach to simultaneously predict Q-values, mean speed, and queue length. The Adam optimizer minimizes a combined loss function.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/8 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase...
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is implemented as a baseline. It fixes the green phase length and calculates the red phase length for the current signal cycle based on the previous red phase and downstream occupancies. The method uses a proportional-integral control law with specific regulator parameters and a desired mainline occupancy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao...
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO. The simulation models a freeway network in Qingdao, China, including a one-lane on-ramp, a three-lane mainline, and a merging area. Speed limits for the mainline and on-ramp are defined, and driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data. The simulation runs from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL and baseline methods in simulation
nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Twenty simulation experiments are conducted for each of three scenarios: DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control. Each experiment is initialized with a different random seed. The performance is evaluated by measuring mean vehicle travel times, queue lengths at the on-ramp, and traffic flows downstream of the merging area.

nodes_process.node_name: Conduct perturbation analysis on video data
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data... The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is performed to assess the impact of video data information on control performance. The control area is divided into eight subareas. Information from each subarea (excluding subarea 2, where PI-ALINEA sensors are located) is systematically removed from the original data to create perturbed datasets. Twenty simulation experiments are then run with these perturbed inputs.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 0/2 tools named, all params stated.
